name: Immigrant Visa by Marriage (13(a))

requirement_groups.name: Spouse of a Filipino citizen, reciprocity nationalities

requirements.blocker_text: Requires a legally valid marriage to a Filipino citizen, with evidence the relationship is genuine and subsisting.

The 13(a) is available only to nationals of countries with an immigration reciprocity arrangement with the Philippines; applicants from countries without reciprocity instead use a Temporary Resident Visa (TRV) as the functional equivalent -- there is no practical preference between the two routes beyond this nationality-based gate.
requirements.fix_path: Confirm reciprocity status for the applicable nationality, or use the TRV route if reciprocity does not apply.

evidence_required.document: Marriage certificate (PSA-issued for marriages performed in the Philippines, or report of marriage for those performed abroad)
Probationary 13(a) status for the first year, converting to permanent status upon Bureau of Immigration confirmation the marriage remains valid

outcome.duration_length: probationary for 1 year, then converts to a permanent immigrant status

sources.title: Asia Long Stay -- Philippines Long-Stay Visa and Residency Options, describing the 13(a)/TRV reciprocity gate and the probationary-to-permanent conversion structure

notes: STATUS: DRAFT. HONEST SOURCING GAP: no direct fetch of a Bureau of Immigration page was achieved for this route in this research pass. STRUCTURAL FINDING: the probationary structure -- 1 year of provisional status before the Bureau of Immigration confirms the marriage is genuine and subsisting and converts the status to permanent -- is a real, deliberate safeguard against sham marriages, structurally similar in intent to Italy's marriage-authenticity screening documented elsewhere in this dataset, though implemented as a formal waiting/conversion period rather than an upfront interview-based test. Marriage to a Filipino citizen does not by itself create permanent residence -- multiple sources explicitly warn that the 13(a) application process is still required and not automatic, a common point of confusion worth surfacing clearly on any route detail page. work_rights is 'restricted' rather than 'full': 13(a) holders generally still need separate work authorisation to be employed, despite being married to a citizen -- distinct from several other countries in this dataset (e.g. Poland's spouse-of-citizen routes) which grant automatic full work rights to a citizen's spouse.
